info.name: ZKT Integration API v1
info.description:
The Integration API (`/api/v1`) for other software: HR, payroll, access control. Contract: `docs/integration-api.md` in the repository.

Generated 2026-11-02 by `tools/postman/integration-collection.php`. Every live `/api/v1` route is here; the generator refuses to run if one is missing.

**Setup**
1. Collection → Variables: set `base_url`, and `email` / `password` for signing in (or paste a token into `token`).
2. Run **0. Start here → Sign in**: the token is saved for every other request.
3. Ids are variables (`employee_code` = Personnel ID, `device_id`, …). Requests that create something save its id for the next request.

**Conventions**
- Envelope: `{success, message, data, meta, errors}`. `401` no/bad token, `403` missing ability or permission, `404` not found, `422` validation (reason per field in `errors`), `429` rate limit (120/min per token).
- Times are UTC ISO-8601.
- Anything that touches a terminal answers `202` with a command or session: **queued, not done**. Poll it.
- Writes accept an optional `Idempotency-Key` header (disabled by default in each request).

⚠ **This is a live system.** Requests marked *Talks to a real terminal* write to real hardware. Default ids point at the test employee (Personnel ID 90110121) and IT ROOM (15).

exec: const how = { token: 'run 0. Start here → Sign in', command_id: 'send a request that queues a command first (Push, Start enrollment, …)', session_id: 'run 3. → Find enrollment session (for this command) first', new_department_id: 'run Create department first', webhook_id: 'run Create webhook first', delivery_id: 'run List deliveries first', token_id: 'run Create token first', run_id: 'copy an id from List attendance sync runs' };
if (pm.request.auth === undefined || pm.request.auth === null || pm.request.auth.type !== 'noauth') { names.push('token'); }

for (const n of names) { if (n === 'token' && pm.info.requestName.startsWith('Sign in')) { continue; } const v = pm.variables.get(n); if (v === undefined || v === null || String(v).trim() === '') { throw new Error('{{' + n + '}} is empty: ' + (how[n] || 'set it under Collection → Variables') + '. (If it is filled under Variables, check no Environment is selected, top right.)'); } }

item.name: 0. Start here
item.description:
Sign in, then check the token. Every other request sends `{{token}}` as a Bearer token.

For software that runs unattended, do not use a person's sign-in: create a scoped token for a service user on the server (`php artisan integration:token <email> <name> --ability=…`) and paste it into the `token` variable.

header.description: Optional. Repeat a timed-out write with the same key: the first answer comes back and nothing runs twice.

request.description:
Signs in a website user and stores the token in `{{token}}`. A sign-in token carries every ability (`*`) but is still limited by that user's permissions.

Set the collection variables `email` and `password` first (Collection → Variables). They stay on your PC.

**Body fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `email` | email | yes |  |
| `password` | string | yes |  |
| `device_name` | string | no | A label for this token, e.g. `postman`. |

Answers who you are, which company (tenant) and the token's abilities. Use it to check a token works.

**Answer:** `200`. `401` = no or bad token.

The abilities a token can carry and what each grants:

| Ability | Grants |
|---|---|
| `employees:read` | employees, departments, access levels |
| `employees:write` | create / change / delete employees, departments, photos |
| `devices:read` | terminals, commands, sync runs, enrollment sessions |
| `devices:write` | push/remove people, enroll, trigger syncs, retry/cancel commands |
| `attendance:read` | punches, summaries, reports |
| `webhooks:manage` | webhooks (the user also needs `settings.manage`) |

item.name: 1. Employees
item.description:
Create, read, change and delete employees.

**Every employee URL takes the Personnel ID** (`employee_code`, e.g. 90110121), which is also the user ID on the terminals. Answers still show the system's own `id` beside it; you never need it. `external_id` is your system's id, if you keep one.

Every response uses the envelope `{success, message, data, meta, errors}`. `422` = validation, with the reason per field in `errors`.

request.description:
Creates one employee. **Answer:** `201` with the employee; its Personnel ID is saved to `{{employee_code}}`, so the next requests address the new employee.

The example body passes validation as it is. It uses `{{new_employee_code}}` and `{{new_external_id}}`; change them before a second run, since both must be unique.

**Body fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string ≤255 | yes | First name(s). On POST only; on PUT/PATCH send only what changes. |
| `last_name` | string ≤255 | no |  |
| `employee_code` | string, digits, 1–9 | no | Personnel ID (CPR). Leave out and the next free one is allocated. Unique per company. Becomes the user ID on terminals. |
| `external_id` | **string** ≤128 | no | YOUR system's id for the person. Must be text: `"1"`, not `1`. Unique per company. Never sent to a terminal. |
| `gender` | `male` \| `female` | no | Lowercase. |
| `birthday` | date `YYYY-MM-DD` | no | Before today. |
| `email` | email | no |  |
| `mobile_phone` | string ≤32 | no | Digits, spaces, `()` and `-`, optional leading `+`. The website stores `"+973 33445566"`. |
| `home_phone` | string ≤32 | no | As mobile_phone. |
| `department_id` | integer | no | A company or a department from `GET /departments` (e.g. 4 = PROMOSEVEN). Must exist. |
| `job_title` | string ≤255 | no |  |
| `hired_date` | date | no |  |
| `employment_type` | `full_time` \| `part_time` | no | Default `full_time`. Do not send `""`. |
| `resigned_at` | date, today or earlier | no | **Setting it makes them inactive and queues their removal from every terminal.** Leave out for a current employee; `null` to clear. |
| `privilege` | `user` \| `enroller` \| `admin` \| `superadmin` | no | Role on terminals. Leave out for a normal user. |
| `device_password` | string, 1–8 digits | no | Keypad password on terminals. Write-only: never returned. |
| `card_number` | integer 0–4294967295 | no | Stored; reaches a terminal only through a push. |
| `access_level_ids` | array of integers | no | From `GET /access-levels`. Send `[]` for none, never `""`. |
| `multi_card_group_id` | integer | no | Must exist; leave out when not used. |
| `valid_period_enabled` | boolean | no | When true, both dates below are required and **to must be after from**. |
| `access_valid_from` | date | no |  |
| `access_valid_to` | date | no | After access_valid_from. |
| `office, education, country, city, postal_code, political_status, race` | string | no | Free text. `country` is the English name, e.g. `"Bahrain"`. |

| `push_to_mapped_devices` | boolean | no | Update only: re-push to every terminal they are on now. |

query.description: Also take them off every terminal.

request.description:
Without the flag: deletes the record only, **the person stays on the terminals** and can still punch. Prefer **Delete by Personnel ID**.

With `remove_from_devices=1`: `202`; removals are queued per terminal (card and fingers saved first), the employee is inactive at once and deleted only after every terminal confirms. A failed removal keeps the record, inactive.

> ⚠ **Talks to a real terminal.** Check `{{device_id}}` before sending.

item.name: Delete by Personnel ID (system AND terminals)

header.description: Optional. Repeat a timed-out write with the same key: the first answer comes back and nothing runs twice.

request.description:
Deletes the employee **and always takes them off every terminal**; there is no record-only form. Card and fingerprints are saved into the system before each terminal delete.

- `200` + `meta.deleted: true`: on no terminal, deleted at once.
- `202` + `meta.deleted: false`: removals queued (`meta.device_commands`); deleted once every terminal confirms.
- `404`: no employee has that code.

`data` = `{id, employee_code, name}` of who it was. Check it is the person you meant.

> ⚠ **Talks to a real terminal.** Check `{{device_id}}` before sending.

item.name: 2. Terminals and pushing people
item.description:
Terminals (devices), and putting people on them or taking them off.

**Check `capabilities` on a terminal before offering an action**: not every model can do everything (the C3 panels cannot write users or capture fingers).

request.description: Every terminal with `is_online`, `is_writable`, `write_refusal` and `capabilities` (`confirmed` / `implemented` / `not_implemented` / `unknown` per action).

request.description:
Queues writing this person onto this terminal: name, role, keypad password, and the card and fingers the system holds for them. A first push gives them their Personnel ID as the terminal's user ID (or the next free number when it is taken there).

No body.

> ⚠ **Talks to a real terminal.** Check `{{device_id}}` before sending.

item.name: 3. Fingerprint and card enrollment
item.description:
Enrollment needs **a person at the terminal**. The call returns at once with a **command**; when it runs, it opens a **session** and the terminal waits for a finger (~30 s) or a card tap (~20 s).

Session `status`: `pending → sent → waiting → success | timeout | failed | cancelled`. `timeout` means nobody came, not a broken terminal.

The person must be on the terminal first (**Push employee to terminal**).

header.description: Optional. Repeat a timed-out write with the same key: the first answer comes back and nothing runs twice.

request.description:
Puts the terminal into capture mode for this person. **Be at the terminal**: press the same finger 3 times, lifting it in between.

**Answer:** `200` with the **command** that starts the capture; its id is saved to `{{command_id}}`. The enrollment **session** is created when that command runs, a second later: then run **Find enrollment session (for this command)** until `status` is `success`. `409` = a capture is already waiting for them there. `422` = this terminal cannot capture fingers.

**Body fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `finger_slot` | integer 0–9 | yes | 0–4 left hand little→thumb, 5–9 right hand thumb→little. **6 = right index**. |


> ⚠ **Talks to a real terminal.** Check `{{device_id}}` before sending.

item.name: 8. Webhooks
item.description:
Instead of polling, this system calls **your** URL when something happens. Needs `webhooks:manage` and the `settings.manage` permission.

Each call is signed: `X-Webhook-Signature: sha256=HMAC_SHA256(secret, "{X-Webhook-Timestamp}.{raw body}")`. Verify it, reject timestamps older than ~5 minutes, dedupe on `X-Webhook-Id`. Delivery is at-least-once and not ordered.
